summary: Tested backend APIs (/api/bot/status, /api/accounts), bot.py handler logic with mocked MEGA service and fake Telegram Update/Context objects, and the frontend dashboard. Handler tests ran against an isolated throwaway Mongo DB that was dropped afterwards. All 13 pytest tests pass, in serial and with xdist. In the dashboard, all required testids render, the empty state shows, and a test account inserted then refreshed shows the masked email, save folder, free space and usage bar. No console errors.

minor.issue: If auto_switch is ON and every account's storage refresh fails, pick_account_for returns None. refresh_storage(None) then raises TypeError, so the user gets 'Link save nahi hua ... NoneType' instead of a clear message. pick_account_for also never uses its size argument.
ms.storage(m) is a synchronous network call made directly in the async handler (not wrapped in asyncio.to_thread). It blocks the event loop, including FastAPI, while MEGA responds.

Folder callbacks always act on the current active account. If the user switches accounts and then taps a button on an older folder message, list_folder silently falls back to root on the wrong account, and 's:' saves that account's root as the save folder.
If the account was already removed, acc is None and the user sees a raw 'Error: NoneType object is not subscriptable'.

integration_issues.issue: load() has no try/catch or loading state. If an API call fails, the promise rejection goes unhandled and the status card stays on 'Load ho raha hai...' forever with no error shown. The refresh button gives no busy feedback.

action_items: Optional: wrap ms.storage(m) in cmd_addaccount with asyncio.to_thread
Optional: handle pick_account_for returning None (all accounts unreachable) with a clear message
Optional: add try/catch plus a loading/error state to the frontend load()
Optional: guard the rc: callback against a missing account
critical_code_review_comments: accounts_view refreshes storage for every account one after another on each /accounts or button press. This is slow with many accounts; consider asyncio.gather.
Folder callback buttons do not carry the account id, so actions on an old message can hit a different account after a switch.
seed_data_creation: None persisted. Handler tests use throwaway DBs named TEST_bot_handlers_<uuid>, dropped after each test. API and UI tests inserted one TEST_ account into test_database.mega_accounts and deleted it by id; verified the count is back to 0.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/. Handler tests import bot and mega_service directly, monkeypatch ms.run, ms.login_check and ms.storage, and set bot.db to a fresh motor DB inside asyncio.run (no pytest-asyncio is installed). Never start a second polling instance; @Mega_handler_bot is live. No real MEGA credentials are available.
